comparison_targets: RP-2592 / STRAT-SPEC-0004 15m SMA crossover trend continuation
RP-3731 / STRAT-SPEC-0005 15m SMA crossover ATR-stop momentum
RP-6236 / STRAT-SPEC-0006 4h SMA crossover ATR-stop momentum

proposed_mechanics.anchor: EMA side condition using ema_lookback_bars 50 or 96, plus candle body/ATR impulse and session context.
proposed_mechanics.trigger: Directional impulse continuation from candle body size relative to ATR, on the EMA side, with RVOL participation.
proposed_mechanics.gate: UTC session hours and weekend exclusion are load-bearing; RVOL minimum is fixed at 1.2.
proposed_mechanics.normalization: Body size normalized by ATR through body_atr_min; no fast/slow moving-average crossover.
proposed_mechanics.entry_logic: Both-direction continuation entries require EMA side, body/ATR impulse, RVOL, and allowed UTC session.
proposed_mechanics.exit_or_risk_logic: ATR stop multiple 2.0 and entry throttle; no opposite SMA crossover exit is proposed.

concluded_family_mechanics.anchor: Fast SMA and slow SMA pair with side-specific trend SMA confirmation.
concluded_family_mechanics.trigger: Fast SMA crosses above slow SMA for long or crosses below slow SMA for short.
concluded_family_mechanics.gate: Side-specific close versus trend SMA confirmation and fixed min_bars_between_entries=16.
concluded_family_mechanics.normalization: No body/ATR impulse normalization and no session/RVOL gate.

concluded_family_mechanics.anchor: Same fast/slow/trend SMA crossover grid as STRAT-SPEC-0004.
concluded_family_mechanics.trigger: Fast/slow SMA crosses with trend SMA confirmation.
concluded_family_mechanics.gate: Fixed throttle; no session or RVOL gate.
concluded_family_mechanics.normalization: Adds fixed ATR-stop exit, but entry remains SMA crossover.
concluded_family_mechanics.exit_or_risk_logic: Opposite SMA crossover exits plus fixed ATR stop.

concluded_family_mechanics.anchor: Rescaled 4h fast/slow/trend SMA crossover grid inherited from STRAT-SPEC-0005.
concluded_family_mechanics.trigger: Fast/slow SMA crosses with trend SMA confirmation on 4h bars.
concluded_family_mechanics.gate: Fixed throttle; no session or RVOL gate.
concluded_family_mechanics.normalization: Adds fixed ATR-stop exit, but entry remains SMA crossover.
concluded_family_mechanics.exit_or_risk_logic: Opposite SMA crossover exits plus fixed ATR stop.

mechanical_differences: HYP-004R has no fast/slow moving-average crossover trigger.
HYP-004R uses EMA side as context, not fast SMA crossing slow SMA as the event.
HYP-004R uses candle body relative to ATR as the impulse trigger.
HYP-004R uses RVOL and UTC session windows as gates; the concluded momentum targets do not.
HYP-004R declares session_hours_utc as a denominator axis and weekend_allowed=false, making session selection load-bearing.
HYP-004R proposes ATR stop only as risk/exit context, while RP-3731/RP-6236 use ATR stop on top of SMA crossover entries.
mechanical_overlaps: All compared surfaces are continuation or momentum-adjacent.
HYP-004R and the targets use moving-average context, though EMA side differs from SMA crossover.
HYP-004R, RP-3731, and RP-6236 mention ATR in risk/normalization surfaces.
load_bearing_fresh_elements: ema_lookback_bars is an explicit denominator axis and uses EMA rather than fast/slow SMA pair crossing.
body_atr_min is an explicit denominator axis and defines impulse strength.
session_hours_utc is an explicit denominator axis and weekend_allowed=false is fixed.
RVOL participation is required at rvol_min=1.2.
The absence of fast/slow crossover mechanics is central to distinctness.
cosmetic_elements: Momentum and continuation wording overlaps with concluded families.
ATR-stop language overlaps with RP-3731/RP-6236 but is not the entry trigger.
Moving-average context alone is not enough for freshness; distinctness depends on no crossover trigger and load-bearing session/impulse/RVOL gates.
reason: The proposed surface does not reduce to the concluded SMA crossover families as written because it uses EMA-side context, body/ATR impulse, RVOL, and UTC session filters instead of fast/slow SMA crossing. Collapse risk is medium because a future formalizer could accidentally express a generic moving-average momentum or crossover wrapper; that would invalidate this result.
